newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Beacon signals raises hopes for British yachtsman.
newsitem.headline: Beacon signals raises hopes for British yachtsman.

text.p: Australian rescue officials held out hope on Tuesday that a missing British round-the-world yachtsman may be alive after noticing a change in the signal from his distress beacon.
"We are very, very hopeful that Tony Bullimore is alive inside the hull of his yacht," Australian Maritime Safety Authority spokesman David Gray told Reuters.

Bullimore, 56, and 29-year-old Frenchman Thierry Dubois sent out distress calls late on Sunday after sailing into a storm in the Southern Ocean about about 1,400 nautical miles (2,600 km) southwest of Perth.
Dubois was believed to be safe aboard a life raft coping with heavy seas after he was found standing on the hull of his upturned yacht, Amnesty International, on Monday.
Gray said distress beacons used by competitors in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race had two positions, and one of Bullimore's beacons had been altered overnight.
"That can only be activated by a person or by a freak wave moving something around in the cabin," Gray said.
An airforce search aircraft was expected to be in position over Bullimore's listing yacht, Global Exide Challenger, at about 10 a.m. (0200 GMT).
Frenchman Dubois clambered aboard a life raft dropped by a rescue plane on Monday, only for it to capsize and take water, but managed to reach a raft dropped by a second plane.
"He's having trouble keeping his life raft upright," said Gray. "The seas are pretty bad...and the only way you can right it when you are on your own is to get out in the water."

Dubois, about 40 km from Bullimore's yacht, faces another two days in the life raft until he is reached by Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS Adelaide, which left Perth on Monday equipped with a Seahawk helicopter.
Australian maritime officials have also diverted a Cape Town-to-Sydney-bound Liberian-registered tanker, the Sanko Phoenix, to the area, which will also arrive on Thursday.
Gray said weather conditions were little changed with 50 knot westerly winds and a five metre swell.
The two yachtsman hit difficulties about 120 nautical miles south of the region where French yachtsman Raphael Dinelli was rescued from his sinking yacht two days after Christmas.
The rescue mission was the longest rescue Australian authorities had attempted for yachtsmen, Gray said. The Australian coast is more than 2,500 kms (1,500 miles) away.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a large-scale rescue mission to save French yachtswoman Isabelle Autissier, who was competing in the BOC Round-the-World Yacht race.
